bluf: The Goat Agency is a European influencer and creator agency selling creator first content joined to paid media; its headline claim is that it is the only globally scaled influencer agency, with 650 staff across 37 markets in 2025. It publishes dated case studies at pace, two dated 15 September 2026, and advertises its own FMCG creator guides on LinkedIn and Google. The record lists no moves, news, jobs or pricing, and its site runs no social ad pixel while it sells paid social. A rival should know the book is almost all observed creator work with a thin measurement layer: that is the line to attack.
doing:
Its positioning line, an award winning global influencer agency championing a 'human media revolution' and pairing creator first content with connected media so brands can Influence Everywhere, decodes to a plain offer: find and brief creators, produce the content, buy media behind it. The headline claim, the only truly globally scaled influencer agency with 650 staff across 37 markets in 2025, is quoted from its about page, which also claims firsts in paid creator media and in influencer content inside Amazon's DSP.

The sold mix is narrow. The services page lists Strategy, Discovery, Content, Media, Commerce and Measurement & Optimization and names one proprietary product, IBEX, function not shown. The capability read scores Creator & Influencer at 3, the lead line, on the note of 16 influencer campaign case studies; Paid Social at 2, core, on the note that it claims it first ran paid media through influencers' own channels; Data & Measurement, Programmatic & CTV and Retail Media at 1 each with no evidence note. The one partner listed is YouTube, on an AI powered influencer solution per the about page.

AI posture: no AI service offer; the YouTube partnership claim is the only AI line, and the AI need on two client rows reflects the clients' products (IBM's LLM, Dell's AI).

The record lists no moves and no news, only a case study cadence: Dell on 3 July 2025, Heineken and IBM on 5 September 2025, Calvin Klein on 6 February 2026, Kraken Rum on 6 May 2026, John Deere and Asahi Super Dry on 15 September 2026. The John Deere TikTok work is credited with Gold at the Digiday Media Awards and Silver at the Shorty Awards.

Pricing: the record lists no pricing signal. Conspicuously absent for an agency claiming 37 markets: no HQ city or office list, unknown ownership, no jobs or ATS, no evidence behind Measurement & Optimization, no owned audience line.
clients:
Client type: enterprise, in FMCG, food and beverage, alcohol, technology, gaming, fashion, beauty, automotive, entertainment and agriculture; region Europe, no HQ listed; case studies describe US and EMEA work (Dell, IBM) and a Goat North America unit.

The needs read lists 18 client rows, all case studies: 16 observed and 2 names only. Social and creators sits on 15 rows, Brand and creative on 8; AI, B2B, leads and organic demand on 1 or 2 rows each. Observed signals: John Deere (social plus organic demand, a creator to front its TikTok channel) and Asahi Super Dry (social, a claimed 46% engagement rate and Bronze at the 2026 Global Influencer Marketing Awards), both dated 15 September 2026; Kraken Rum, brand, 6 May 2026, awareness for the Gold Spiced range; Calvin Klein, social, a Q4 holiday campaign, 6 February 2026; Minor Figures, brand plus social, the Hyper Oat launch, 28 January 2026; Heineken (brand plus social, a creator launch party) and IBM (B2B plus social plus AI, promoting its LLM), both 5 September 2025; Mars Wrigley, social, the Crispy Rolls comeback, 21 August 2025; World of Warcraft, Arla (Cravendale) and Arm & Hammer, 19 August 2025; Odeon, social, a slug only. The two names only rows are Qualcomm and Qualcomm (Snapdragon), although the Coachella case study dated 10 December 2025 describes creator work.

Four clients sit on other tracked books: Heineken (artefact), Mars Wrigley (msq), John Deere (mod-op), Qualcomm (code-and-theory). Only 2 of its 18 clients are names only. Next: under KJ8 (Human provenance becomes a distribution signal) it is likely these brands will ask for labelled human creator provenance; under KJ5 (The price of attention splits in two) there is a roughly even chance, moderate confidence, that they push for measurement beyond engagement rate, which the record cannot answer.
house: Say and do: three sold lines tested. Paid Social is contradicted: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site, the flagged gap. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated by its own LinkedIn ads (24+), Creator & Influencer by its own short form channels (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube). Tag stack: gtm and complianz on WordPress; no social pixels, test tools or ABM stack. The sitemap lists 291 URLs, 46 updated in 90 days and 145 in 365 days. It publishes an llms.txt and blocks no AI crawlers. Its Transparency Center record shows 25 Google ads, 12 in the last 30 days, 24 text and 1 image, advertiser Goat Solutions LTD, last shown 27 September 2026. The LinkedIn Ad Library shows 24 company page ads and 0 thought leader ads, a floor since 772 ads match the name query; sample: 'The ultimate influencer marketing guide for FMCG brands'. Meta and TikTok status is not read.

openings:
Lead with the observed contradiction: it sells paid social and its own site runs no social ad pixel, so a rival with its own pixel stack opens on the say/do gap. The strongest judgment follows: it is likely, moderate confidence, that its enterprise FMCG and alcohol accounts (Heineken, Mars Wrigley, Asahi Super Dry, Arla, Minor Figures) are contestable on measurement, because P4 is partial and the only figure any case study excerpt quotes is Asahi's 46% engagement rate. Falsifier: a dated case study, or a described IBEX function, reporting paid media outcomes beyond engagement.

Second, price: with no public pricing model (P5 unknown), a transparent outcome priced creator offer is a conversation it cannot have in public; very likely usable, low confidence on buyer weight. Third, KJ5 exposure through Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV: the connected media half of its offer is the hours that judgment removes, so creator content with cheaper distribution and holdout measurement undercuts it. Heineken (artefact), Mars Wrigley (msq), John Deere (mod-op) and Qualcomm (code-and-theory) sit on other tracked books and are likely contestable. Hard to beat: creator scale, score 3 and 16 case studies; almost no chance a rival out claims it there.

The case studies dated 15 September 2026 (John Deere, Asahi Super Dry) and blog posts dated 28 September 2026 show the publishing machine running; follow whether IBEX gets a described function or a measurement case study appears.
